title: Help for Individuals Affected by Bank-related Cyber Scams or Unauthorised Bank Transactions
what_it_is: Help for Individuals Affected by Bank-related Cyber Scams or Unauthorised Bank Transactions

sections.label: Consumer liability for fraudulent transactions
sections.summary: Consumers who act responsibly are protected from losses from fraudulent transactions, with liability caps for lost cards and non-card e-payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Generally, consumers who have suffered financial losses from fraudulent transactions are protected as long as they have acted responsibly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For online card transactions, if a merchant has not adopted a system which requires consumers to authorise transactions using one-time passwords (OTPs), a consumer will not be liable for an unauthorised transaction.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: For lost or stolen cards, a consumer’s liability is capped at $100 for lost or stolen cards, provided he or she has not been careless and has reported the loss promptly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Likewise, for non-card e-payments, consumers who have practised proper cyber hygiene and have not been negligent will not be liable for any losses arising from unauthorised transactions that do not exceed $1,000.

sections.label: Police and IMDA investigations
sections.summary: Police and IMDA are investigating these specific cases to determine what happened and find the root cause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: One, Police and IMDA are investigating these specific cases that have arisen and they will find out, try to determine what exactly has happened so that we can get to the root of it.

sections.label: Payments Council framework review
sections.summary: The industry, through the Payments Council, is reviewing the framework to clarify cases where both institution and consumer deny fault.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Thirdly, as I also highlighted, we are working with the industry through the Payments Council to review the framework to provide greater clarity should instances arise where both the financial institution and consumer say, "Look, we did not do anything" and the consumer says, "I never revealed any OTP", as what Ms Yeo said her residents claimed.

sections.label: Review timeline by year-end
sections.summary: A review and outcome are being worked towards by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the third question, on the timeline, we are working towards a review and an outcome by the end of the year.

sections.label: Holistic approach to fraud prevention
sections.summary: The issue will be looked at holistically to assure consumers while balancing incentives for all parties to prevent fraudulent transactions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I wonder if the Minister can elaborate on legislative efforts along this front.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But we will look at it holistically and see how best we can move forward on this issue, providing assurance to consumers but also ensuring a balance of incentives for all parties to do their part in preventing fraudulent transactions.
